question.text: Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, the NAV calculated on each Valuation Day for a closed-ended Category II AIF must be disclosed to investors:

answer.text: Only at the end of each financial year

explanation.text: The Logic: Per PDF Section 11.10: 'NAV calculated on each Valuation Day shall be disclosed to all investors on a QUARTERLY basis for closed-ended AIFs.' This matches Cat I/II AIF close-end structure (where inflows/outflows are episodic, not daily). The Trap: Daily applies to Cat III (open-end / continuous NAV); weekly is not standard; annual is too infrequent. Cat I/II closed-end: valuation at least 6-monthly (Reg 23), NAV disclosure quarterly. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) tests daily NAV. XIX-A tests quarterly disclosure. The 'valuation frequency' (6-monthly) vs 'disclosure frequency' (quarterly) is a common confusion point — keep them distinct.
